newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt state offers to sell KABO majority.
newsitem.headline: Egypt state offers to sell KABO majority.

text.p: The Egyptian state said on Tuesday it was willing to give up majority control of partially privatised Kabo /Nasr Clothing and Textiles.
The official Holding Company for Spinning and Weaving last month offered investors at least 10 percent or 306,200 shares in Kabo. The deadline for bids was May 29.
"The offer until May 29 was three times oversubscribed. Then the state decided it wanted to get out of the firm totally," a corporate source said.
The state said in a published announcement it was putting on offer 63 percent or 1.93 million shares in Kabo and was extending the deadline for receiving bids to Thursday, June 5.
The minimum bidding price is still 109 pounds and investors can buy up to 5,000 shares. The Commercial Bank of Egypt and its Commercial International Investment Company are the agents for the sale.

The holding company now owns 70.05 percent of Kabo, which makes garments under its own label and for several international brands like JIL, Jockey, British Home Stores and Wrangler. Private investors own 29.95 percent of the firm.
The corporate source said the state would sell to Kabo's employees the shares that remained in its holding after the public offer.

Stock exchange figures showed Kabo made after-tax profits of 6.872 million pounds ($2.02 million) in the first nine months of the financial year 1996/7, against 2.868 million in the same period of 1995/6. The years start July 1.
